dedupe_keys.name: netherlands 12 week pilot of proactive ambulance relocation policies in a dispatch centre

description: This case study evaluates dynamic ambulance relocation in live operation at a Dutch ambulance dispatch centre. The authors, from Centrum Wiskunde en Informatica and the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, developed two policies that move idle ambulances in real time to keep good coverage of the region, which an ambulance service provider in the Netherlands adapted for operational use and built into a software tool for real-time decision support. The policies were used by dispatchers in a pilot lasting 12 weeks. The article, published in 2018 in the INFORMS Journal on Applied Analytics, describes the relocation methods, evaluates the pilot with statistics on efficiency gains and discusses the experience of dispatchers and managers; an author version is free to read online in the Vrije Universiteit repository. Coverage is one dispatch region. Caveats: the region and service are described in the article, not the abstract, the pilot is short and the operational data are not public. Based on the pilot's success, the policies were adopted for continued use and permanent implementation by the service, aiming to reduce late arrivals against response time targets. Simulation uses: evidence that relocation policies can move from simulation into practice, for ambulance coverage and dispatch models. Related records: the Region Zealand response time trends (case_study-region-zealand-ambulance-dispatch-response-time-trends) and the Lazio base simulation (case_study-lazio-ares-118-ambulance-location-des) are other European ambulance studies.
